---
title: "Start here: Students"
description: >
  A path for graduate students: Fit, check and explain an IRT model for a
  course or thesis, with figures a committee will accept.
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

You need to fit an IRT model for a course or a thesis, check that it holds up,
and explain it in figures and plain words. mirtverse does the bookkeeping so
you can spend your time on the interpretation.

## Your path in three steps

**1. Learn the ideas with the book and the labs.** The free online book
[*Item Response Theory with mirt and mirtverse*](../book/index.html) has one
chapter per week of a typical course, from
[classical item analysis](../book/measurement.html) to
[reporting results](../book/reporting.html). The
[interactive labs](teaching-labs.html) let you practise on realistic data:

```r
library(mirtverse)
run_lab("model-choice")   # Lab 1: Choose a model a certification board can defend
```

**2. Run your own analysis.** Choose a model, read what it means, and check
the items:

```r
sel <- select_model(mydata)   # compares Rasch, 2PL and 3PL and explains the choice
mod <- sel$best
interpret(mod)                # what the results mean, in plain language
item_table(mod)               # item statistics, fit and flags in one table
```

Prefer clicking? `launch_workbench()` does the same steps with buttons and
writes the R code for you, which you can paste into your thesis appendix.

**3. Make figures and a report.** Every plot is a ggplot2 object, so you can
restyle it for your university's template:

```r
gg_wright(mod)                               # person-item map
gg_info(mod)                                 # test information
mv_report(sel, file = "thesis-analysis.html")   # everything in one file
```

The [Gallery](gallery.html) shows what each figure looks like.

## Keep going

- [Glossary](glossary.html): Nearly 90 IRT terms in plain language.
- [Cheat sheet](../cheatsheet/mirtverse-cheatsheet.pdf): The main functions on
  two printable pages.
- [Which IRT model?](which-model.html): A one-page flowchart from your item
  scores to a model and the code that fits it.
- [Coming from ltm, eRm or TAM?](mirtify.html) `mirtify()` rewrites your old
  code as mirt code.

## Writing it up

The [thesis kit](thesis-kit.html) walks from data to a finished Methods
paragraph. `cite_methods(mod)` drafts that paragraph in APA style, with the
software versions, model, estimation, fit, reliability and references, so
you only have to check and edit it:

```r
cite_methods(sel, sample = "undergraduate students", file = "methods.docx")
```

Cite mirt (Chalmers, 2012) and mirtverse in your methods section;
`cite_methods()` adds both references for you.
